paper_title: Constraints on Axion-like Particles from a Hard $X$-ray Observation of Betelgeuse
coupling_convention: canonical g_agamma in GeV^-1, as plotted (lower dashed edge of red band, most optimistic model)
notes: Astrophysical ALP-photon conversion bound from NuSTAR hard X-ray observation of Betelgeuse. 95% C.L. upper limit g_agamma < (0.5-1.8)e-11 GeV^-1 for m_a < (5.5-3.5)e-11 eV, depending on Galactic magnetic field model and stellar model. Conservative: g<1.8e-11 for m_a<3.5e-11 eV; optimistic: g<5.2e-12 for m_a<5.5e-11 eV. Limit is approximately flat below the turnover mass. Not a DM haloscope, so no local density assumption. | selector: figure_vision over text (quality (1, 1, 1, 1, 2, 0, 0.7, 16)) | Vision: Fig. 3 shows NuSTAR Betelgeuse red band. Text states 95% C.L. limits g_agamma < 5.2e-12 GeV^-1 (optimistic, tcc=3.6yr, BT=3.0uG) for m_a<5.5e-11 eV, and < 1.8e-11 GeV^-1 (conservative, BT=0.4uG) for m_a<3.5e-11 eV. I traced the lower (optimistic) boundary of the excluded red band. The boundary is a plateau at low mass then rises steeply near 5.5e-11 eV.
